what: Matsyendra's Kaula teaching — body as the place of the divine, centres, nectar, conquest of death, secrecy — carried into the Nāth tradition

evidence.detail: Nāth lineages place Matsyendra, bringer of the Yoginīkaula, at their head.
Nectar, centres, khecarī-type practice and kāla-vañcana in both KJN and GŚ.

what: Shared siddha names and songs (Mīna/Matsyendra, Jālandhara, Kāṇha, Cauraṅgī, Virūpa, Carpaṭi) and the eighty-four-siddha frame

evidence.detail: sahaja, śūnya, twilight language in Nāth and Buddhist siddha songs.
Varṇaratnākara's list of 84 mixes Nāth and Buddhist names; HYP 1.5–8 includes Virūpākṣa, Carpaṭi, Kānerī.

notes: U49 owns the full treatment of the overlap.

what: The haṭha corpus ascribed to Gorakṣa and the siddha lineage at the head of the Haṭhapradīpikā

evidence.detail: HYP 1.1–9 names Ādinātha, Matsyendra, Gorakṣa and the Nāth siddhas as its source.

what: Nāth initiation and yoga through Gahinīnāth to Nivṛtti and Jñāneśvar

evidence.detail: Jñāneśvarī 6.291 ('nāthasaṅketa') and the closing lineage ovīs of ch. 18.

what: The vocabulary and imagery of sahaj, śūnya, anahad nād, gagan maṇḍal, the tenth door and ulaṭbāṃsī used by Kabīr and other Sants

evidence.detail: Gorakh Bānī imagery (inverted well of nectar, sky-circle) recurs in Sant songs.
Kabīr–Gorakh Goṣṭhī stages the relation as debate.

what: Gorakṣa (Korakkar) and Matsyendra (Macchamuni) among the eighteen Tamil Siddhars

evidence.detail: Tamil Siddha lists include Korakkar and Macchamuni.

notes: Whether these are the same figures or homonyms is disputed; U22 owns the Tamil side.

what: The cult of Matsyendranātha as Karuṇāmaya (Buṅga-dyaḥ) and the legend of Gorakṣa's drought

evidence.detail: Newar legend of bringing Matsyendra from Kāmarūpa; see dsp:identity-of-matsyendra.

what: Encounter narratives (Allama and Gorakṣa) and possibly the figure of Revaṇasiddha

evidence.detail: Śūnyasampādane and Prabhuliṅgalīle stage the meeting.

what: The goal of the perfected, deathless body and siddhas who are also alchemists (Nityanātha, Carpaṭi, Nāgārjuna in some lists)

evidence.detail: kāya-siddhi, rasāyana; the Akulavīra warns against grasping rasāyana.

notes: Metal/mercury practices are restricted; not detailed.

what: Dattātreya as teacher of the Nāths in Marathi tradition

evidence.detail: Navanātha Bhaktisāra; Gorakṣaguṭikā 1.24 names Dattātreya with Gorakṣa.

what: Cremation-ground dwelling, skull bowl and transgression of purity

evidence.detail: Aghorīs are often described by scholars as heirs of the Kāpālikas; the tradition traces itself to Dattātreya and Kīnārām instead.

what: Dattātreya as ādiguru of Aghora; Girnar

evidence.detail: Kīnārām's vision of Dattātreya at Girnar; Kālūrām as Dattātreya.

what: Kīnārām's first Vaiṣṇava initiation and the Rām-language of his works

evidence.detail: Kīnārām initiated by Śivarām; titles Rāmgītā, Rāmrasāl.

what: The doctrine of the eight fetters and non-dual conduct

evidence.detail: Kulārṇava 13.90 list of the eight fetters as cited in Aghora teaching; KJN non-dual conduct.
